blocks.s: Bernard assigns four species of contemplation: admiration of God's majesty (admiratio majestatis), contemplation of his judgments (intuitio judiciorum), consideration of his benefits (consideratio beneficiorum), and inspection of his promises (inspectio promissorum). Each of these is a distinct mode of the soul's elevated gaze upon the divine reality: the first corresponds to the second species treated in Book One, concerning the incomprehensible divine majesty; the second to the mysterious and inscrutable ways of divine providence; the third to the benefits of the Incarnation and Passion and the grace poured into souls; and the fourth to the glory promised to the blessed.
